question: TTFT of the 64-token fresh case: 0.79 s in the 13-14.10 f1 matrix vs 0.39-0.42 s in the 16.10 runs

different.sustained_warmup: old matrix: none (one 22-token warm-up request only); 16.10 runs: QWEN36_BENCH_WARMUP_S=60 = 26-27 repeated 16K prefills with 128 forced tokens before the measured cases
different.bench_source_sha256: differs (harness changed between the runs: sustained warm-up and the compare-ab fixes)

cause: Protocol, not code: the 13-14.10 matrix measured fresh_64 as the first heavy request of a freshly started server without the sustained warm-up, and the same 128 tokens / 18.25 GB of expert H2D took 0.78 s of engine prefill GPU time instead of 0.41 s once 26 repeated 16K prefills had warmed the GPU and the PCIe/expert path; stock bf128 in the old matrix shows the same effect (0.75 s), the installed f1 runtime and the new-tree L0 agree in 16.10 (0.42 vs 0.39 s).
caveat: The data proves the protocol difference and that the extra time is engine prefill GPU time (not client or queue time); that the mechanism is GPU clock/PCIe warm-up is the consistent explanation but was not isolated by a clock trace.
